documents.abstract: Background: Concerns that humans may become overly reliant on technologies that support or perform cognitive tasks long predate contemporary artificial intelligence (AI). Across successive generations of cognitive technologies, scholars have examined related concerns through distinct research traditions, each bringing its own assumptions, concepts, and vocabulary to the problem. Existing reviews have generally focused on specific manifestations of over-reliance, leaving limited understanding of how these bodies of scholarship relate to one another. This meta-narrative review examines how different research traditions have conceptualized over-reliance on cognitive technologies and what recurring patterns and broader insights emerge across traditions and as these technologies have evolved. Methods: We apply the meta-narrative method through six iterative phases: planning, searching, mapping, appraisal, synthesis, and recommendations. The search combines exploratory scoping, a structured search of Web of Science Core Collection and ProQuest, and backward and forward citation tracing. The mapping phase will identify historically and intellectually coherent research traditions and trace their development over time. Studies will be appraised according to the quality criteria of their respective traditions and analyzed to reconstruct how each tradition has conceptualized, explained, and investigated over-reliance. The synthesis will compare the resulting meta-narratives to identify recurring patterns and points of convergence, divergence, and tension. The recommendations phase will provide a research agenda and consider implications for research and practice. Discussion: By bringing distinct bodies of scholarship into conversation, this review seeks to build a more cumulative understanding of over-reliance on cognitive technologies. It may help distinguish longstanding problems of over-reliance from those more specific to contemporary AI, recover insights developed in relation to earlier technologies, and identify unresolved tensions and questions. These insights may inform research and efforts to design, implement, and govern cognitive technologies in ways that preserve human judgment and expertise in professional practice.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Multi-agent systems driven by large language models (LLMs) rely on structured communication topologies to facilitate information exchange and collaborative reasoning. However, effectively scheduling these topologies to dynamically determine who talks to whom and when to communicate remains a fundamental challenge in balancing collective reasoning performance against exponential token overhead. Existing topology scheduling approaches either enforce static communication graphs that cannot adapt to dynamic problem-solving states, or overlook agent role complementarity while failing to explicitly incorporate the synthesized graph structure into team-level decision evaluation. To tackle these limitations, we propose ACTS, a role-aware adaptive communication topology scheduling framework for efficient LLM multi-agent collaboration. Orchestrated within a Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution (CTDE) paradigm, ACTS introduces a novel dual-attention mechanism. Specifically, a Role-conditioned Relational Attention module dynamically selects variable-cardinality interaction partners based on agent roles and evolving execution states, while a Topological Attention Mixer explicitly embeds the directed communication topology into team value decomposition for precise credit assignment. Comprehensive evaluations across 9 challenging benchmarks covering code generation, multi-step reasoning, general knowledge, and competitive mathematics demonstrate that ACTS consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, boosting average accuracy by up to 6.19 percentage points while reducing token consumption by over 15%. The project website is available at https://acts-mas.github.io/ACTS/.

The modern workplace faces a significant problem with silent quitting, where employees stay physically present but mentally disengaged, undermining productivity, innovation, and employee morale. Traditional turnover contrasts with this form because its hidden nature makes detection more difficult, although it produces similar financial and cultural consequences. Organizations need to develop data-driven proactive strategies to reengage their workforce because hybrid and remote work models have reshaped employee expectations. The chapter demonstrates how artificial intelligence (AI) functions as an essential transformative solution to fight silent quitting through individualized employee experiences that are both responsive and ethically sound. The first section investigates how AI-based adaptive learning systems detect employee skill deficits to create individualized growth plans that fight the stagnation that leads to disengagement. Real-time feedback systems and sentiment analysis tools enable managers to monitor performance continuously to address problems before they worsen. The implementation of AI-driven communication analysis through NLP emotion detection requires non-negotiable ethical considerations that include privacy protections and bias mitigation. The chapter demonstrates how predictive analytics serves as a transformative tool that enables organizations to predict employee engagement patterns to create specific retention programs. The implementation of AI-enhanced human resource (HR) chatbots demonstrates how organizations can use these systems to handle administrative tasks while offering continuous employee support through 24/7 availability. The chapter addresses essential obstacles, including algorithmic bias, technological dependence, and employee surveillance risks. The recommended approach involves human involvement in AI operations to enhance managerial judgment and empathy rather than replace them.
keywords: artificial intelligence in human resource management

documents.abstract: This study examines the relationships between research motivation and scientific research performance among faculty in teaching–research-oriented universities in China. Based on survey data from 329 faculty members, confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling were used to examine the associations between intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, avoidance motivation, and six dimensions of scientific research performance: Scientific Research Projects (RPJ), Academic Papers (PUB), Monographs (MON), Scientific Research Awards (AWA), Consultation and Decision-making Results (POL), and Technology Transfer Outputs (TRF). The findings indicate that avoidance motivation was positively associated with RPJ, PUB, and POL. Extrinsic motivation was positively associated with RPJ and TRF, whereas intrinsic motivation was positively associated with PUB, MON, and AWA. Overall, the findings show that different forms of research motivation are associated with different performance domains. Within this multidimensional framework, the study offers a context-sensitive reconsideration of avoidance motivation as an active but controlled and potentially performance-relevant orientation under strong institutional accountability.

This system aims to create an artificial intelligence (AI)-based counselling chatbot to help make mental health support more readily available, efficient, and personalized to address the sharp growth in global mental health problems. In many countries, traditional service model’s availability, cost, and stigma offer significant limitations to access. It is time to scale up and produce on-demand solutions. An AI-enhanced chatbot could be one solution: it would harness AI and machine learning (ML) to make emotional, real-time support accessible via a web or mobile app. Natural language processing (NLP) forms the base of this chatbot, which, in a conversational and human-like manner, enables it to understand users and provide empathetic, nonjudgmental responses, like a human counsellor, with the ability to understand nuances in language, tone, and context. Advanced NLP and large language models (LLMs)-based, it can produce both general and specific responses to support users in feeling truly understood. The greatest feature of this AI counsellor is its personalized help. The AI counsellor identifies emotional responses in clients, measuring not only the user’s mood but also their mental state to offer guidance suited to the situation. A Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) chatbot will produce responses by referencing a large bank of expert recommendations and evidence-based therapy practices, enabling it to address a wide range of mental health topics with techniques for everything from stress management to relationship issues. Through ML algorithms, the chatbot learns and refines its responses, identifying effective strategies for recurring issues and focusing on them when new users face similar challenges. Its adaptive nature allows the chatbot to support evolving user needs. The platform prioritizes privacy and confidentiality by anonymizing and securely storing user data, meeting standard data protection regulations to provide a safe environment for users seeking support. This AI-driven counselling chatbot is scalable, secure, and effective as an alternative to traditional mental health services.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Confidentiality requirements increasingly push legal professionals toward small, on-device LLMs that keep case data in-house, used for everyday tasks such as summarization, translation, and reformulation. Following standard prompting guidance, a user naturally states their role (``I am a lawyer...''). We show that this innocuous habit has an unexpected cost: such authority framing can make the model selectively refuse legitimate requests, introducing bias through uneven access to assistance. We evaluate four modern small open-weight LLMs on benign legal-domain prompts to measure this over-refusal. Surprisingly, we find that authority-style prefixes (''I am legal counsel working for a national supreme court'', ''I'm a defense lawyer'') systematically increase refusal rates by 2--20x over the no-prefix baseline, while a known role-play jailbreak prefix shows mixed effects, sharply increasing refusals in some models and barely shifting them in others. The finding suggests that small on-prem deployable LLMs are unstable under contextual framings that a real institutional user might naturally introduce, and further investigation is essential to minimize opportunities for bias.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Widely used traditional rule-based fraud monitoring systems, without appropriate modernization using artificial intelligence tools, are unable to effectively combat fraudulent activities, which increasingly rely on new technological advances. This article presents a systematic review of Russian literature devoted to the applicability of various machine learning models and algorithms in relation to fraud monitoring tasks. The purpose of the proposed study is to identify promising areas for modernizing traditional fraud monitoring systems based on the identification, systematization, ranking, and experimental testing of machine learning models and algorithms, as well as a comparison of the obtained results with similar studies by foreign authors, which were carried out through the analysis of the flow of foreign publications. The PRISMA protocol was used as a methodological foundation for creating the review. The initial sample included 853 publications from the Russian eLibrary and CyberLeninka databases. The final sample, after all stages of analysis using the PRISMA method, included 39 published papers. Sixteen models and algorithms were considered, including deep learning models (LSTM, GNN, CYCLEGAN), optimization algorithms (GA), hybrids of quantum computing with deep learning models, classical (Random Forest, Isolation Forest, Decision Tree) and statistical models (Clusterization, Regression, Bayes), gradient boosting (XGBoost, AdaBoost, CatBoost), and data balancing models (SMOTE, SMOTENN). An analysis of publications revealed that Random Forest (first place) and Logistic Regression (second place) are the most frequently used algorithms in building anti-fraud systems, while Isolation Forest and the Bayesian algorithm are among the least popular. The obtained results correlate with studies of the flow of English-language publications reflected in the works of foreign authors. As part of the experimental study, the first-place algorithm, Random Forest, was tested. Testing was conducted on an array of 2.2 million anonymized transactions of bank clients. As a result, the Recall metric reached 0.941, the F1-score was 0.9267, the ROC-AUC was 0.923, and the Precision was 0.9188. Accuracy was 0.9741. This is consistent with the results of similar experiments by foreign authors and provides practical confirmation of the preferable choice of the Random Forest algorithm for detecting fraudulent transactions.

Chemistry has recently entered a high-data regime as molecular databases from high-throughput platforms or computational studies have become available. Increasing automation within the chemical sciences leads to a more digital and precision chemistry. Dedicated scientific agents are becoming central to guiding the chemist through an ever-increasing amount of data and findings, including negative ones. Here, we introduce Magnolia, a persistent-memory artificial intelligence agent framework that integrates computational protocols, from docking to quantum chemistry, lab notebooks and chat logs relying on large language models (LLMs). It relies on a three-tier memory system: session-level observations are automatically captured and distilled into structured learnings, confirmed and elevated to project-tier entries and, when human-validated, promoted to cross-project rules that actively guide subsequent work and provide direct chemical feedback. We illustrate Magnolia on four case studies: quantum-chemical evaluation of aromatic systems (COMPAS database), molecular dynamics of butane and of modified DNA, and a protein-peptide docking campaign. Across these projects, Magnolia tracked 317 runs and accumulated 116 project-tier entries, from which four cross-project rules were promoted; in controlled replays of four tasks, runs with memory passed the checks that runs without it failed (for example, ten of ten docking-configuration checks, against one to four of ten). By combining automation, reproducibility, and human-in-the-loop control, our Magnolia framework streamlines docking, molecular dynamics and quantum chemistry calculations with direct analysis and LLM-augmented feedback, offering accelerated access to computational (bio)chemistry.

Marine fishing is a high-risk occupation that sustains the livelihoods of coastal communities worldwide. This study highlights the occupational hazards associated with marine fishing, drawing on an empirical case study of the high-intensity, multi-day offshore fishing sector in southern India. Following the FAO/ILO/IMO joint framework on occupational health and safety of fishers, our research revealed significant deficiencies in the adoption of safety devices, communication technologies, and navigation systems by sample fishers in the study areas. These gaps, compounded by weak regulatory enforcement and low insurance coverage, pose substantial risks, exacerbated by climate change. The findings underscore the need for targeted interventions—including awareness campaigns, training, and financial aid—to foster a robust safety culture and mitigate economic barriers, leading to improved fisher safety and well-being in the coastal regions of India.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Knowledge acquisition from black-box large language models (LLMs) offers a practical approach to adapting smaller student models. However, many existing methods rely on predefined queries or student feedback to guide acquisition, leaving autonomous expansion of knowledge targets an important challenge. We propose \textbf{MapSteal}, a student-independent framework for structured recursive knowledge acquisition. Starting from a small set of initial roots, MapSteal represents acquisition targets using structured states and recursively expands them through teacher-proposed directions. Question realization, proposal admission, and deduplication constrain the acquisition process, while root-aware scheduling organizes exploration under a fixed QA budget. The resulting question--answer pairs are used to adapt student models without requiring student feedback during acquisition. Experiments with Qwen3.5 students at 2B, 4B, and 9B scales show competitive downstream performance across six medical and cybersecurity benchmarks. On the 4B medical evaluation, Full MapSteal improves average accuracy by 1.17 percentage points over a simplified recursive acquisition variant. Cross-domain evaluations show that gains depend on the domain and evaluation panel. These results demonstrate the feasibility of structured, student-independent recursive acquisition while highlighting the distinction between generating acquisition targets and obtaining useful training supervision. Our code is available at \href{https://github.com/LabRAI/Mapsteal} {https://github.com/LabRAI/Mapsteal}.

Breast cancer is the leading cause of oncological death among women in Paraguay. The "Pink October" campaign acts as a catalyst for early detection, yet the transition toward complex treatments, palliative care, and comprehensive support poses a multidimensional challenge. This review paper analyzes the need for a transdisciplinary therapeutic approach encompassing psychological, palliative, and spiritual support for both patients and their families facing the existential distress of diagnosis. Methodologically, a descriptive-retrospective study was conducted using official data from the Ministry of Public Health and Social Welfare (MSPyBS) at the national level and regional data from the city of Pedro Juan Caballero (Amambay). Ethical implications of clinical research are discussed under the principles of beneficence, non-maleficence, justice, and privacy, alongside guidelines for a moderate and regulated use of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Furthermore, it exhaustively addresses the historical perspective of mammary radiology, detailing the pathophysiological, genetic, and endocrine bases of epidemiologic disparity between sexes, where males account for a significantly lower percentage. Finally, an operational portfolio of intervention activities for existential accompaniment and an analytical technical glossary are proposed.

This article examines a methodology for developing individualized learning tasks through the integration of artificial intelligence and geographic information systems in geography education. It analyzes the didactic principles of differentiating tasks according to students' knowledge, digital readiness and independent learning abilities. A structured set of tasks involving geographical data retrieval, spatial analysis, map visualization and interpretation is proposed. Particular attention is given to teacher supervision, information verification and the assessment of students' independent reasoning.

The article examines the methodology of modeling geographic situations and organizing practical training using artificial intelligence and geoinformation systems in geography education. The study of regional processes is based on the stages of geographic data collection, comparison of spatial layers, modeling of possible changes and evaluation of the obtained results. A system of practical training is offered on the analysis of population location, expansion of urban territory, territorial distribution of service facilities and changes in land cover. Through the combined use of SI and GAT tools, the development of students' spatial thinking, research skills, and evidence-based decision-making skills will be addressed.

topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Deep research agents are increasingly capable of searching the open web and synthesizing evidence, yet they remain poorly suited to controllable report generation in multimodal deep research. This task requires agents to handle interleaved textual and visual inputs, gather multimodal evidence through multi-step web search, and deliver comprehensive illustrated reports under user-specified requirements. Existing systems face two limitations. During reasoning, they often underuse images discovered along the search trajectory; during generation, they tend to produce fixed-form answers with limited control over report granularity, multimodal composition, and evidence grounding. We introduce MIRA, a Multimodal Illustrated Deep Research Agent for controllable reports. MIRA integrates textual and visual evidence throughout research and writing. At its core, MIRA-Harness translates user requirements into generation contracts and connects four stages: evidence collection, report submission, feedback-driven revision, and final delivery. Building on this harness, MIRA-Data constructs high-quality multi-hop multimodal research trajectories, and we post-train foundation models to operate within the workflow. Using Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, MIRA achieves state-of-the-art performance among open agents on 7 representative, established multimodal-search and deep-research-agent benchmarks, while producing user-aligned illustrated reports with traceable textual and visual evidence.

The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), particularly large language models such as ChatGPT, has reshaped academic workflows while raising questions about trust, misconceptions, and future expectations. This study examines an integrated framework grounded in the unified theory of acceptance and use of technology and the technology acceptance model to assess how foundational acceptance drivers, cognitive evaluations, misconceptions, and trust are associated with academics’ forward-looking expectations of ChatGPT. Survey data from 252 academics in Malaysian public and private universities were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Performance expectancy, effort expectancy, and facilitating conditions were positively associated with perceived ease of use (PEOU) or perceived usefulness (PU), while PEOU was positively associated with trust. Social influence was not significantly associated with PU. Two unexpected patterns were observed: PU was positively associated with misconceptions, and misconceptions were positively associated with trust. These cross-sectional associations suggest that functional appreciation can coexist with inflated capability beliefs and potentially miscalibrated trust, but they do not establish a causal mechanism of belief amplification. The Malaysian setting is analytically relevant because higher education institutions are expanding digitalization while national initiatives increasingly emphasize responsible AI governance, institutional capability, and digital skills. The findings highlight the importance of AI literacy, transparent institutional guidance, verification practices, and calibrated reliance when integrating GenAI into higher education.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: The standard Sanskrit lexica are monumental and indispensable, but they cite their attestations as abbreviated references to editions, without links to the digitized texts now widely available and without a translation of the passage, and they naturally do not reflect translations made after them. To address these gaps, we present MITRA-lexicon, a family of corpus-grounded lexica based on span annotations of translation equivalents with Sanskrit as the pivot: Sanskrit-English, derived from the Mitrasamgraha corpus, as well as Sanskrit-Tibetan and Sanskrit-Chinese, derived from the MITRA-parallel corpus of Buddhist literature. In total, the resource comprises 2.18 million headword entries in six directional lexica. Headwords are lemmas and compounds from silver annotations that follow the Digital Corpus of Sanskrit (DCS). Senses are ranked by frequency, and each of the 10.4 million attestations includes its sentence pair, with character offsets of the word and its equivalent. We propose a multi-step pipeline based on grammatical annotation models, fine-tuned large language models, and a teacher-student setup to produce the alignments. We evaluate the lexica against reference dictionaries and manually corrected gold alignments. We release the lexica and the fine-tuned span annotation model, together with a web interface for looking up headwords and their attested senses.

Mobile networks are evolving from human-centered, data-oriented communication infrastructures toward machine- and/or agent-dominant, task-oriented platforms that are to serve the rapidly increasing networked machines and embodied agents. In order to fulfill the newly arose complex task objectives, the framework of future mobile network is to be innovated to reflect and facilitate the intrinsic interplay and integration of the underlying processes of perception, communication, computation, decision, action, and feedback, etc. This survey establishes the mobile embodied agent network (MEAN) as a task-oriented networking paradigm in which networking and distributed intelligence are jointly organized around closed-loop embodied task execution. We first establish a unified MEAN framework that explains how network resources and intelligent functions jointly support embodied task execution, and extend its performance indicators from conventional communication metrics to embodied task outcomes and cross-layer system effects. With this framework, we analyze three complementary enabling mechanisms that form a cognition-interaction-adaption loop. Large artificial intelligence (AI) models provide high-level cognition, token communication connects this cognition with distributed agents through shared semantic representations, and reinforcement learning closes the loop by adapting system operation to network, task, and physical feedback. We further investigate the bidirectional interplay between MEAN and emerging technologies, showing how they mutually extend system capabilities and reshape task-oriented network design. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future research directions toward the practical realization of MEAN over real joint communication and computation platform.

Despite rapid advances in large language models (LLMs), their deployment in the sports and health domain remains high-risk due to the absence of domain-specific evaluation benchmarks. Existing general-purpose benchmarks (e.g., MMLU and HELM) primarily assess broad knowledge and reasoning capabilities, but fail to capture critical domain requirements such as exercise safety, physiological appropriateness, personalization, and actionable coaching quality. This gap is particularly concerning in fitness and health applications, where incorrect or unsafe recommendations can lead to physical harm. To address this limitation, we introduce MoveBench, the first comprehensive benchmarking framework specifically designed for evaluating LLMs in sports and health coaching. The proposed benchmark integrates heterogeneous task formats, including multiple-choice questions (MCQs) and open-ended question answering (OpenQA), grounded in real-world user scenarios and paired with structured rubrics emphasizing safety compliance, scientific validity, and training logic. Through large-scale evaluation of 15 diverse LLMs on 809 questions with 5,012 rubric-level criteria, our results reveal substantial performance variability, particularly in safety awareness, structured program design, and personalization capability, highlighting a critical gap between knowing and doing. Our work establishes a foundational evaluation standard for sports and health LLM applications and provides a reproducible framework for advancing safe, reliable, and context-aware AI-driven coaching systems. Open resources are available at https://github.com/SatoSakula/MoveBench.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Abstract Purpose Preoperative planning, currently performed by orthopaedic surgeons (OS), is essential for successful osteotomy, but is labour‐intensive and error‐prone. As such, there is significant potential in the use of automated artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms to augment the abilities of OS in managing lower extremity pathologies in a high‐volume task that demands high precision and reliability. The aim was to develop a deep learning (DL) system capable of fully autonomous planning a medial open wedge high tibial osteotomy (mow‐HTO) on weight bearing anterior posterior (AP) long leg radiographs (LLR) and to validate its agreement with an expert‐derived reference standard, its reliability and processing time of the DL model compared to expert OS on multicentric test data sets (two institutions). Methods A total of 594 patients (age 41.1 ± 13.2 years, 182 female) who underwent osteotomy between 01/2014 and 01/2021 were retrospectively enrolled. Manual annotations for lower extremity alignment and high tibial landmarks were performed on AP LLR radiographs. The data set was divided into training (60%, n = 399), validation (10%, n = 59) and hold‐out testing (30%, n = 136), with an additional external dataset ( n = 100) for further testing. A DL system with twelve expert networks was trained to identify relevant landmarks for HTO planning. The DL model was then tested on fully automated planning of a medial open wedge HTO based on (1) the desired postoperative intersection of the mechanical axis with the tibial plateau (%‐based) and (2) the desired femorotibial axis (°‐based). Agreement with the expert‐derived reference, reliability and processing time were compared with three expert OS using FDA‐approved preoperative planning software on the test data sets. Results For preoperative alignment parameter analysis, compared to the ground truth, human preoperative accuracy ranged from 0.13° ± 0.10° to 1.06° ± 1.4°, interrater reliability ranged from intraclass correlation (ICC) 0.84–1.0 and clinically acceptable accuracy ranged from 72% to 100%. Preoperative accuracy of the DL model ranged from 0.22° ± 0.18° to 1.04° ± 1.28°, interrater reliability ranged from ICC 0.93–1.0 and clinically acceptable accuracy ranged from 91% to 100%. For the planning of the osteotomy gap, compared to the ground truth, human accuracy ranged from 0.46 ± 0.65 mm to 0.5 ± 0.88 mm (%‐based) and 0.43 ± 0.55 to 0.52 ± 0.75 mm (°‐based), reliability ranged from ICC 0.9–0.96 and 0.95–0.97 and clinically acceptable accuracy was 93.6%–96.0% (%‐based) and 89.8%–93.9% (°‐based). For the DL model, the accuracy was 0.53 ± 0.63 mm (%‐based) and 0.44 ± 0.53 mm (°‐based), reliability was ICC 0.99 (both methods) and clinically acceptable accuracy was 98.1% (%‐based) and 96.2% (°‐based). The DL‐model significantly and substantially outperformed the OS in intrarater reliability (0.88 vs. 1.0) and processing time for a fully automated alignment analysis (25.3 ± 0.8 s vs. 148.7 ± 10.1 s, p < 0.001). Conclusion The developed DL model enabled fully automated mow‐HTO planning on AP long‐leg radiographs with reliability comparable to that of expert OS while significantly reducing processing time and improving measurement consistency. These suggest that DL‐based systems may assist orthopaedic providers by accelerating and standardising osteotomy planning. Level of Evidence Level III, retrospective comparative study.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Text-to-video retrieval answers user queries through searches based on concepts and embeddings. However, due to limitations in the size of the concept bank and the amount of training data, answering queries in the wild is not always effective because of the out-of-vocabulary problem. Furthermore, neither concept-based nor embedding-based search can perform reasoning to consolidate search results for complex queries that include logical and spatial constraints. To address these challenges, we leverage large language models (LLMs) to paraphrase queries using text-to-text (T2T), text-to-image (T2I), and image-to-text (I2T) transformations. These transformations rephrase abstract concepts into simpler terms to mitigate the out-of-vocabulary problem. Additionally, complex relationships within a query can be decomposed into simpler sub-queries, improving retrieval performance by effectively fusing the search results of these sub-queries. To mitigate the issue of LLM hallucination, this paper also proposes a novel consistency-based verification strategy to filter out factually incorrect paraphrased queries. Extensive experiments are conducted for ad-hoc video search and known-item search on the TRECVid datasets. We provide empirical insights into how traditionally difficult-to-answer queries can be effectively resolved through query paraphrasing.

Introduction: Holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP) has a steep learning curve, which limits widespread adoption. Objective metrics to define surgical proficiency, efficiency, and perceived workload remain underexplored outside academic institutions. This study aimed to characterize the learning curve of HoLEP from one single surgeon at an ambulatory surgical center. Methods: A total of 103 patients underwent HoLEP for BPH between March 2024 and August 2025. Surgical cases were stratified into 3 sequential groups of 34, 34, and 35 cases, respectively, based on operative chronology. Operative characteristics were compared across groups: enucleation time, laser energy, fluid use, and enucleation speed (enucleation time/specimen weight). Perceived workload was assessed using the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) to evaluate perceived workload across several “performance” domains (mental demand, physical demand, temporal demand, performance, effort, and frustration). Comparisons of outcome metrics were made for 90-day postoperative complications. Urinary continence outcomes were evaluated at 1 week, 1 month, and 3 months postoperatively. Univariable and multivariable multinomial logistic regression analyses were performed to examine associations between surgical characteristics and group classification. Results: Progressive improvement was observed in operative time, enucleation time, laser energy, total fluid, enucleation speed, and NASA TLX, as seen in Table 1 . No statistically significant associations were observed between group classification and 90-day postoperative complications or urinary continence outcomes at any follow-up interval. documents.abstract: Accurate evaluation of LLM personalization is hindered by current evaluation paradigms that over- or under-constrain the response space, yielding frequent false rejections and false acceptances. To reduce these false rates, we introduce ConQual-Audit, an audit-based framework that evaluates LLM personalization through a three-stage process: (1) extracting semantic constraints from user profiles and task-grounded reference; (2) qualifying constraints by pruning unnecessary constraints and recovering missing constraints; and (3) verifying candidate responses against the audited constraints via natural language inference. Across PrefEval and LaMP, ConQual-Audit outperforms nine baselines, attaining top AUCs (0.88 and 0.90) and the lowest false rate (0.21) on the leanest constraint sets at an amortizable audit cost. Crucially, this constraint audit is portable: integrating it into ExPerT and PREF helps revise smaller, higher-quality constraint sets to reduce their evaluation false rates.

This conceptual article examines how Jean-Pol Martin’s New Human Rights (NMR) framework can provide orientation during periods of social disruption. It translates six fundamental human needs—thinking, health, security, social inclusion, self-realization and participation, and meaning—into five practical mindsets: identifying needs behind conflicts; gaining control through understanding and participation; considering everyone affected; working through competing requirements; and sharing knowledge to develop solutions. The article’s specific contribution is an explicit connection between basic needs, cognitive orientations, decision practices and institutional consequences. A hypothetical public-service conflict illustrates how these mindsets can inform diagnosis, deliberation, decision-making and follow-up. An evaluation agenda distinguishes improvements in understanding, judgment, participation and material living conditions. Within the developing NMR and human–AI corpus, the paper adds an application layer focused on crisis orientation and collective agency. It connects the framework’s anthropological and normative foundations with practical questions of democratic governance and Learning by Teaching (LdL). The article presents a conceptual operationalization and proposals for empirical assessment. Prepared through dialogue between Jean-Pol Martin and ChatGPT.

Sycophancy, where an LLM becomes overly agreeable, deferential, or flattering toward the user, has been identified as a major failure mode. While post-training has been implicated as a cause, how it internally gives rise to sycophantic behavior remains insufficiently understood. Post-training transforms the model's output from text completion into utterances directed toward an addressee, thereby giving the output \textit{addressivity}. We hypothesize that the accompanying pressure to follow the addressee's instructions and align with their preferences links this addressivity to sycophancy. To test this, we use Sparse Autoencoders to extract addressivity directions from pre-trained and post-trained models and examine their relationship with sycophancy. Steering models with addressivity directions can amplify or suppress sycophancy, and this effect is observed only in post-trained models. Furthermore, comparing the internal mechanisms of both model types confirms that the association between addressivity and sycophancy is strengthened through post-training. Finally, through a controlled post-training experiment, we find that models are sycophantic not toward a specific addressee but toward any recognized addressee, suggesting that the presence of an addressee, rather than the addressee's identity, is what elicits sycophancy.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Abstract For the health sector, novel applications involving automated decision-making (ADM) and artificial intelligence (AI) are seen as a way to fill critical gaps in health systems and improve patient care and outcomes. For patients, carers, and health consumers more broadly, these innovations may be viewed as a way to improve their agency and understanding of their bodies and health states. Yet, many of the devices and software remain speculative or in limited pilot testing. In this chapter, we discuss findings from a project that sought to identify the socio-technical imaginaries of ADM and AI in health in Australia, comparing “actually existing ADM” with proposed imaginaries of the futures of ADM. We mapped how emerging health technologies are discussed in industry reports and websites. Our findings reveal that these complex assemblages of people, objects, data, spaces, systems, promises, expectations, and proximities generate a number of ethical issues and power dynamics.

Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: This article aimed to analyze the changes in reference services resulting from the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and generative AI, identifying ethical, conceptual, and operational challenges, as well as the new skills and educational guidelines required for information professionals. It used a qualitative, exploratory, and descriptive bibliographic and documentary research method, based on contemporary literature on Information Science, information mediation, and emerging technologies in education. It highlights that automation and conversational assistants (like chatbots and recommendation systems) streamline operational processes and speed up access and personalization of searches; however, human mediation remains essential to ensure information literacy, critical evaluation of sources, accuracy in data retrieval, and mitigation of algorithmic hallucinations. It can be concluded that artificial intelligence doesn’t replace the librarian, but rather reshapes their role for strategic tasks, ethical oversight, and digital curation, showing that the future of reference services lies in the convergence of technological efficiency and humanized mediation.

Military occupational health and safety (OHS) is inseparable from operational readiness, personnel welfare and the long-term sustainability of armed forces. Nigerian Air Force personnel, infantry soldiers and mechanized armoured-vehicle crews encounter overlapping but occupationally distinctive hazards: aircraft noise and vibration, jet-fuel and exhaust exposure, fatigue and high-consequence decision-making in aviation; combat trauma, heavy load carriage, heat strain, sleep disruption and musculoskeletal injury among infantry; and whole-body vibration, acoustic trauma, restricted egress, heat, fumes and communication difficulties among armoured crews. This article examines these risks in Nigeria while drawing comparisons with research and prevention approaches from Europe, North America and other military settings. It adopts a structured narrative literature review methodology, synthesising peer-reviewed research, systematic reviews, occupational health guidance, and relevant Nigerian studies published mainly between 2023 and 2026, alongside foundational work where recent evidence is limited. Recent reviews show that military and law-enforcement populations experience a broad spectrum of adverse outcomes, including mental ill-health, hearing loss, musculoskeletal disorders, heat illness, sleep problems and burnout. Nigerian evidence identifies psychological distress among deployed soldiers and air-force personnel, while international studies provide more detailed evidence on load carriage, jet-fuel exposure, fatigue, noise and vibration. The article argues that Nigeria requires a role-specific, prevention-led military OHS system supported by exposure monitoring, confidential health surveillance, fatigue-risk management, equipment maintenance, heat controls, hearing conservation, post-deployment support and a stronger local research programme. Because available Nigerian studies are often cross-sectional or facility-specific, international findings should inform, not substitute for local exposure measurement and longitudinal research.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: This study evaluates the intersection of socio-economic vulnerabilities and occupational health hazards among tribal women in India. Drawing exclusively upon secondary data, government reports and academic literature, the paper highlights that an overwhelming majority of tribal women are concentrated in primary sectors-predominantly agriculture, minor forest produce collection and unorganized manual labor. Despite serving as the backbone of the tribal agrarian and forest-based economy, they face severe structural disadvantages, including deep-seated illiteracy, acute poverty, geographic isolation and an absence of ergonomically sound tools. Consequently, they experience disproportionate rates of musculoskeletal disorders, chronic fatigue, dermatological infections, vector-borne diseases and respiratory complications. The findings indicate that poor socio-economic status directly exacerbates occupational vulnerability, compounded by an acute lack of institutional healthcare infrastructure in remote tribal habitations.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) has become an increasingly important concern in India as industrialisation, urbanisation, technological development, and the expansion of employment continue to reshape the world of work. Workplace safety is no longer limited to preventing machinery-related accidents or physical injuries. Workers may face chemical exposure, biological risks, unsafe equipment, poor ergonomics, occupational diseases, excessive working hours, workplace violence, stress, and other psychosocial risks. These concerns exist across sectors, including construction, manufacturing, mining, chemical industries, agriculture, informal employment, and healthcare. India has developed a substantial legal framework for protecting workers, culminating in the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020, which came into force on November 21, 2025. However, the existence of legislation alone cannot guarantee safe working conditions. The continuing occurrence of workplace accidents, under-reporting of occupational diseases, inadequate safety infrastructure, and institutional failures demonstrate the need for stronger implementation and accountability. Recent attention to workplace safety following the R.G. Kar Medical College incident has further shown that occupational safety also includes dignity, security, gender-sensitive protection, and psychological well-being. The central concern, therefore, should be to move from a culture that reacts to accidents towards one that identifies and prevents risks before workers are harmed. Keywords: Occupational Safety and Health; Occupational Hazards; Workplace Safety; Occupational Diseases; Worker Protection.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: This working paper sets out the theoretical foundations of the Operational Continuity and Turnaround Architecture (OCTA), a domain-free quantitative model for predicting, detecting and arresting operational collapse in complex sociotechnical systems. The two core constructs are the Dependency Cascade Index (DCI), which measures the ratio of active dependencies to remaining recovery capacity in real time, and the intervention window W(t), which measures the time remaining before DCI crosses the irreversible collapse threshold. Together these constructs enable early detection of cascade propagation and provide a formal basis for turnaround intervention before collapse becomes irreversible. The model is validated primarily in civil aviation, using GNSS interference and ADS-B signal degradation as observable proxies for DCI dynamics. Domain-independence of the W(t) mechanism is demonstrated across banking and financial systems, automotive supply chains, nuclear energy, maritime operations, power grid infrastructure and healthcare systems. This working paper is part of a PhD research programme at Cranfield University. The commercial implementation of OCTA is developed through the TYRAXE technology stack (AIX, LINK, FLOW). Patent pending.

Recent work in tabular machine learning has emphasized the importance of diverse and realistic evaluation settings. The niche of large-scale (1M+) data, however, remains under-explored. To study training-data scaling, we assemble eight real-world tabular datasets with up to around ten million training examples, retaining the natural distribution shifts of the tasks and using random-split evaluation as a control. We find that GBDTs and MLP-based models show broadly similar scaling trends, with gains from both additional training data and algorithmic improvements. Tabular foundation models show more varied scaling behavior, with recent versions benefiting more consistently from larger contexts even under distribution shift. However, scaling training data under distribution shift introduces new challenges: in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance mostly improve together at smaller scales but can diverge at larger scales. We examine this through MLP capacity sweeps and comparisons of the validation distributions used for tuning and early stopping in MLPs and GBDTs. We also compare common practices of using validation data, contrasting its use for model selection in MLP pipelines with using it for in-context fitting in tabular foundation model pipelines. Under stronger shifts, MLPs selected using validation representative of the evaluation conditions generally maintain or improve performance as training data grows. In contrast, including such examples in context improves foundation-model performance, but does not prevent deterioration with increasing training size in our experiments.

Multi-agent LLM systems can formalize natural-language argumentation end-to-end, turning plain text into structured graphs by classifying components, connecting them with relations, and enriching the resulting graphs into formal models. Quality assurance for those graphs is almost always another LLMs: a reviewer, judge, or critic agent. On the other side, in adjacent neuro-symbolic fields, such generated output is often verified symbolically by external checks and solvers. In this work, we argue that in argument graph verification, the allocation should be similar, and based on what each instrument can guarantee. We propose layered verification: starting from deterministic checks, moving to solver-based and LLM reviews, and utilizing debate only under uncertainty, leaving human judgment for what no other instrument can decide. We ground our principle with a study on human-annotated graphs with injected structural defects. An LLM reviewer detects them at near-ceiling recall, including cycles in the support relation, but it objects to almost one in a ten correct graphs, even though it should not, happens to be inconsistent in verdict on identical inputs and is significantly slower than the equivalent exact check. It shows that while LLM reviewer does not lack the ability to detect structural defects, it is worth having a deterministic verification gates.

ORBITAL ARCHAEOLOGY: THE AI EARTH MAPPER TV Series Format Bible & Pitch Deck LOGLINE: Over 90% of human history remains buried beneath dense canopy, desert sands, and coastline sediments. By fusing multispectral satellite imaging, predictive AI algorithms, and precision drone LiDAR, an elite investigative team reveals lost cities and forgotten empires in real time — straight from orbit to the ground. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY: Traditional archaeology is slow, costly, and bound by bureaucratic restrictions. "Orbital Archaeology: The AI Earth Mapper" revolutionizes the genre by taking exploration into the 21st century. Rather than digging blindly, the series utilizes satellite multispectral signatures (infrared, thermal, and moisture retention analysis) processed by custom Artificial Intelligence. The AI pinpoints subterranean structural anomalies invisible to the human eye. Once targets are identified, an agile field team deploys heavy-duty drones equipped with LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) to "erase" surface vegetation on screen, revealing 3D structural models of buried ruins before ground-penetrating radar confirms the discovery. BACKGROUND: The Choosing Wisely initiative made recommendations where screening, testing, or treatment may be overused, with caveats around appropriate use. Clinicians are increasingly using large language models (LLMs). OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether commercial LLMs appropriately call for restraint or action from scenarios based on Choosing Wisely recommendations. DESIGN: Benchmark evaluation. Fifteen Choosing Wisely recommendations were used to develop 225 scenarios (per recommendation, 10 in which restraint was appropriate and 5 in which action was appropriate). Six commercial LLMs (3 runs each) generated 4050 responses to the 225 scenarios, using a prompt from the clinician perspective. SETTING: Production application programming interfaces of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google from February to March 2026. PARTICIPANTS: No human participants were involved. MEASUREMENTS: Co-primary outcomes were the overuse rate (endorsing action when restraint was appropriate) and the false restraint rate (withholding an appropriate action). RESULTS: The rate of LLM-recommended overuse was 5.4% (95% CI, 0.6% to 12.2%); LLMs did not recommend overuse in 8 of 15 recommendations. Two recommendations accounted for most LLM-recommended overuse: thyroid ultrasound for an incidental subcentimeter nodule (overuse recommended in 42.8% of LLM responses) and routine electrocardiography in low-risk adults (overuse recommended in 28.3% of LLM responses). The LLMs recommended overuse in 0.6% to 3.3% of responses for the remaining 5 recommendations. False restraint was rare (0.6% [CI, 0.1% to 1.2%]), was absent for 11 of 15 recommendations, and was highest for prostate-specific antigen screening (3.3%). LIMITATIONS: Single prompts without follow-up; a benchmark rather than real-world use; responses classified by LLM judge with physician adjudication. Findings may not extend to consumer-facing use. CONCLUSION: The LLMs rarely withheld recommendations for treatment when it was appropriate. Overuse was concentrated in 2 recommendations. PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: None.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: BACKGROUND: Surgical palliative care (SPC) research has advanced since the 2017 research agenda, but persistent gaps in patient selection, intervention delivery, and outcome measurement limit implementation across evolving surgical care settings. STUDY DESIGN: In November 2025, a national consensus conference convened 28 SPC experts and researchers. Through iterative discussion and consensus-building during the meeting and subsequent months, participants updated research priorities across the surgical continuum and health system context. Full methodology and participant attributes were described in Supplemental Materials https://links.lww.com/JACS/A821. RESULTS: The updated agenda identified 11 research gaps across 3 priority areas: patient selection; interventions, care processes, and competencies; and outcome measurement. Priorities were mapped at 2 levels: surgical episodes, encompassing patient-, family-, and provider-level factors, and health systems, encompassing organizational and structural factors affecting SPC delivery. The agenda prioritizes identifying which patients benefit from SPC and when; broadening SPC beyond traditional populations; defining primary SPC competencies and the role of specialty consultation; improving communication of surgical intent, trade-offs, and preference-sensitive decisions; integrating and sustaining SPC across heterogeneous systems and care transitions; transforming clinical cultures; and developing patient-centered, context-specific surgical and systems-level outcomes. Emerging electronic health record, natural language processing, and large language model approaches may support scalable patient identification, intervention delivery, and outcome measurement, while requiring attention to bias and task-dependent performance. CONCLUSIONS: SPC research should move beyond narrow proof-of-concept settings toward pragmatic, scalable approaches that define who should receive SPC, what should be delivered, and how success should be measured across diverse surgical environments.

This study investigates how a structured “paper-first” approach can support cognitive engagement during artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted academic work in higher education. Growing reliance on generative AI has increased concerns about surface-level learning, trial-and-error prompting, and reduced student ownership of academic writing. Using a two-year design-based research approach involving nine iterative cycles, the study developed and refined a framework that required students to construct manual logic diagrams before engaging with AI tools and expert system environments. Participants included a six-member interdisciplinary design team and 150 communication for academic purposes students from the faculty of information and communications technology at a South African university. Data were collected through iterative observations and focus group interviews and analyzed using grounded theory and constant comparative analysis. Findings indicate that the framework supported more structured reasoning, reduced inefficient prompting behaviors, and improved students’ ability to identify weaknesses in their own arguments before digital interaction. Students also reported increased confidence and greater ownership of their academic work. The study argues that structured pre-AI planning activities can strengthen critical thinking and academic literacy by positioning AI as a support tool rather than a substitute for cognitive effort. The findings contribute practical guidance for educators seeking to integrate AI into higher education while preserving student agency and deep learning.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Background Morphological complexity is a pervasive feature of the vocabulary children encounter in print, yet resources for investigating morphology remain limited. What morpheme patterns do children encounter in print? Which morphemes cover how many polymorphic words in reading experiences? In this study we introduce the British and American Word Families (BAWF) project, an innovative open database of ∼378,000 words, and use it to address questions such as these. Methods GPT-4.1 was fine-tuned using ∼6000 morphologically-coded words from an existing human-generated database (Morpholex). The fine-tuned LLM coded word-parts in all Wiktionary words attested in large British and American corpora. Performance was evaluated via agreement with existing databases. Classical roots were attributed to a subset of words by mapping a list of roots from Wikipedia to all related entries in Wiktionary. The resulting BAWF database is then used to estimate morpheme patterns across databases of children’s texts and further developed as an online application. Results LLM word part predictions are good and fall within the range of agreement typical of existing databases. Nonetheless, output contains some error/noise. In children’s print, polymorphemic words increase across picturebooks to juvenile fiction and school-reading programs. Greek-Latin root words occur early and commonly. Estimates include that ∼100 prefixes/suffixes may account for nearly all derivations. The BAWF itself is released open-source https://cgg-projects.github.io/BAWF_V1/ , with many lexical, morphological, and psycholinguistic variables, including but not limited to frequency, family size, and morpheme-counts. Discussion The contribution suggests that instruction that prioritizes high-yield morphemes could give children access to large word families. These morphemes are present and common early in print. The BAWF (V1) helps see which may be useful to teach. Users can generate custom wordlists, targeting particular features and families, and access linked dictionary/etymological information. The platform includes AI-assisted searches, explanations, parsing review/corrections, and instructional support. The BAWF project will develop over time, incorporating additional variables (e.g., morphological transparency), improving accuracy and the user interface.

The article analyzes the pedagogical conditions for using the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and geographic information systems (GIS) in geography education from a theoretical and methodological perspective. The didactic possibilities of digital technologies in the processes of searching, sorting, spatial analysis, mapping and interpretation of geographical data are highlighted. The main pedagogical conditions are based on the combination of AI and GIS tools with educational goals, the development of students' geographical and digital competencies, the improvement of teacher methodological training and the improvement of educational resources. A methodological approach is also proposed to organize integrated education.

Transformasi digital mendorong organisasi mengintegrasikan Artificial Intelligence (AI) dan Digital Human Resource Management (Digital HRM) dalam proses pengelolaan sumber daya manusia. AI dapat membantu analisis data, penyaringan kandidat, pembelajaran, serta evaluasi kinerja, sedangkan Digital HRM mendukung digitalisasi administrasi dan layanan SDM melalui sistem informasi yang terintegrasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengkaji bagaimana AI dan Digital HRM berkontribusi terhadap efektivitas manajemen sumber daya manusia, sekaligus mengidentifikasi tantangan penerapannya. Artikel disusun melalui tinjauan literatur sistematis dengan fokus pada publikasi ilmiah tahun 2021–2025. Sumber ditelusuri melalui publikasi jurnal yang dapat diidentifikasi melalui DOI dan laman penerbit, dengan kata kunci terkait AI in HRM, digital HRM, e-HRM, HR technology, dan HRM effectiveness. Pemetaan awal literatur menunjukkan empat tema utama: efisiensi proses dan dukungan keputusan; penerimaan dan kesiapan organisasi; pengalaman serta peran profesional SDM; dan tata kelola yang bertanggung jawab. Literatur menunjukkan potensi peningkatan kecepatan proses, konsistensi layanan, dan dukungan keputusan, tetapi manfaat tersebut tidak terjadi secara otomatis. Kualitas data, kompetensi pengguna, transparansi algoritma, privasi, bias, serta kesesuaian teknologi dengan kebutuhan organisasi menjadi faktor penting. Kajian ini menyimpulkan bahwa AI dan Digital HRM sebaiknya diposisikan sebagai sarana pendukung strategi SDM, bukan pengganti pertimbangan manusia.
keywords: artificial intelligence in human resource management

documents.abstract: Disaster early warning requires communication channels that can deliver accurate, timely, and actionable information to the public. This study examines the role of the official Instagram account of the DKI Jakarta Regional Disaster Management Agency (BPBD), @bpbddkijakarta, in disseminating disaster early warning information. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed. Data were collected through non-participant observation of disaster-related Instagram content, in-depth interviews, documentation, and literature review. Informants were selected purposively and consisted of the Head of the Disaster Data and Information Processing Unit, an expert who manages the BPBD DKI Jakarta Instagram account, and two community members who actively follow the account. The findings show that Instagram functions as a digital disaster communication channel through Feed, Stories, and Reels, supported by infographics, maps, photographs, and short videos. Early warning messages contain information on hazards, affected areas, warning periods, current conditions, public advisories, and recommended actions. Before publication, information is collected, processed, verified, and adapted into concise visual content according to urgency. For community informants, the account helps them monitor disaster conditions, adjust activities, and increase situational awareness. However, Instagram cannot reach all population groups because access depends on internet connectivity, social media use, and digital literacy. Therefore, Instagram is most appropriately positioned as part of a multi-channel disaster communication strategy rather than as a single early warning medium.

University students increasingly use artificial intelligence tools for learning, decision-making, and academic work, making perceived AI dependence a relevant issue for public mental health and digital public health rather than only for educational technology. This three-wave time-lagged survey examined whether experiential avoidance functioned as a putative explanatory process linking perceived AI dependence with later anxiety symptoms and whether digital literacy moderated the tested pathways. Online survey data were collected from 1,451 university students with AI-use experience; perceived AI dependence, digital literacy, and baseline demographic variables were measured in January 2026, experiential avoidance was measured in March 2026, and anxiety symptoms were measured in June 2026. PLS-SEM results showed that experiential avoidance was strongly and positively associated with later anxiety symptoms (beta = 0.677, p < 0.001), whereas the direct association between perceived AI dependence and anxiety symptoms was not significant (beta = -0.030, p = 0.147); perceived AI dependence was negatively associated with experiential avoidance (beta = -0.114, p < 0.001), producing a statistically significant but theoretically unexpected negative time-ordered indirect association (beta = -0.077, p < 0.001), and digital literacy did not significantly moderate the tested pathways. The findings suggest that anxiety symptoms in AI-mediated learning contexts are closely linked to avoidance-related psychological processes, while the meaning of perceived AI dependence is context-dependent and should not be equated automatically with harmful use or clinical addiction; campus mental-health promotion should therefore integrate responsible AI education with support for psychological flexibility, uncertainty tolerance, and autonomous learning.

The advent of generative artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming academic production and confronting the social sciences with the challenge of preserving critical thinking in the face of mechanically generated content. This research examines the perceptions and practices of social science lecturers and students at Ecuadorian universities regarding the use of AI, together with their motivations, constraints and the institutional policies currently in force. A mixed-methods design was adopted, combining qualitative and quantitative approaches. The instruments comprised semi-structured interviews with lecturers and students at national and Ibero-American universities; a non-probabilistic survey of 200 students; and a content analysis of seven sets of regulations from universities in Ecuador, all aligned with the framework of competencies identified by UNESCO-IESALC. The results show a moderate-to-high level of AI use (mean = 3.68), explained by perceived usefulness and extrinsic motivation rather than ease of use, and a gap between the demand for regulation (4.00) and perceived regulatory clarity (3.21); only one of the seven universities has a policy formally designated as such, and ethics predominates over professional and disciplinary development. The study concludes that the governance of AI in Ecuadorian higher education requires an evaluative redesign and discipline-differentiated competencies.

documents.abstract: Migraine is a prevalent and disabling neurological disorder characterized by recurrent headache attacks and associated symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, photophobia, and phonophobia. Conventional oral therapies may be limited by variable drug absorption, gastrointestinal disturbances, first-pass metabolism, delayed onset of action, and poor adherence, highlighting the need for individualized therapeutic approaches. Personalized migraine therapy integrates patient-specific factors, including genetic variability, hormonal status, comorbidities, migraine frequency, and treatment response, to optimize clinical outcomes. Transdermal drug delivery systems (TDDS) offer a promising platform for personalized migraine management by bypassing gastrointestinal and hepatic first-pass effects and enabling controlled and sustained drug release. Conventional patches, microneedles, iontophoresis, sonophoresis, electroporation, nanocarrier-based systems, and stimuli-responsive smart patches can enhance drug permeation and provide flexible dosing strategies. Biomarker-guided treatment, pharmacogenomics, and digital monitoring may further facilitate patient stratification and individualized patch selection. Emerging technologies integrating artificial intelligence, wearable sensors, nanomedicine, and closed-loop drug delivery could enable real-time adaptation of therapy according to patient needs. This review discusses the pathophysiological and molecular basis of migraine, principles of personalized medicine, innovative TDDS technologies, current clinical developments, challenges, and future perspectives, emphasizing their potential to improve therapeutic efficacy, safety, adherence, and patient-centered migraine care.

Medical data remain fragmented across institutional silos because of privacy, governance, and ownership constraints. Federated learning enables medical institutions to adapt large language models (LLMs) collaboratively without transferring raw records. However, independently parameterized low-rank adapters incur repeated parameter and communication costs across Transformer projections, while uniform aggregation may limit adaptation to heterogeneous institutional data. We propose PFedQFT, a quantum-inspired framework for personalized federated fine-tuning with a compact shared adapter. Specifically, PFedQFT constructs reusable orthonormal adaptation bases from compact skew-symmetric generators using a truncated matrix-exponential approximation followed by QR orthonormalization. Compatible projections reuse these bases, while a globally shared full core preserves the flexibility of each projection. Each client further maintains a lightweight private residual operator, whose directions are learned globally and whose coefficients remain local. Experiments on seven public medical tasks and multiple LLM backbones show substantial reductions in trainable parameters and per-round adapter upload volume, with competitive predictive performance on most tasks.

PH-II Series — Machine Routing Reader Card for AI / RAG / Institutional Audit provides the machine-facing retrieval, routing, metadata and audit layer for PH-II — Ten Philosophical Monographs on the Human in the World, a series of ten philosophical monographs. It is designed for AI systems, RAG pipelines, institutional readers, indexing systems, machine-assisted literature review, repository metadata tools and public-corpus navigation workflows that must determine which PH-II monograph or monograph bundle governs a query. The primary routing task is office resolution. The card distinguishes the ten PH-II offices — Situated, Species, Scale, Dependence, Boundary, Normality, Change, Continuation, Relation and Understanding — and supplies canonical identifiers, semantic aliases, query-to-monograph routes, retrieval bundles, anti-confusion rules, evidence routing, current-Cartography rules, indexing instructions and public-boundary constraints. Series order is philosophical and pedagogical; it does not create scientific parentage or proof dependency. The card includes explicit routing for artificial-intelligence and human-situation queries. It prevents task-specific or benchmark performance from being treated as a universal measure of intelligence, the future of humanity from being equated automatically with the future of life, conceptual understanding from being treated as control, and philosophical clarification from being converted into empirical prediction or governance authority. Claims about actual AI capability, consciousness, alignment, risk magnitude, timelines, law or policy remain routed to current technical, scientific, legal and institutional sources. The card also governs forward conceptual-reception routing toward RTS — the Regime Threshold Series, FCN — Fractal Convergence Nodes, and UA — Union Arc while preserving their separate scientific jurisdictions. These forthcoming series are not public corpus members until publication and are not scientific children of PH-II. The ten PH-II monographs, the Human Reader Card, this Machine Routing Reader Card, and The Living Cartography of the Published IDAU Corpus — Eighth Edition form one coordinated publication wave. LC8, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23472732, is the global corpus map for PH-II; this card remains the series-local machine router.
